label: canon-c19-in12-sharp-tb
_why: THE TIE-BREAKER of canon_c19_in12_sharp_n2.json: the third run of the 2+1 rule, launched ONLY when alignment_check.mjs exits 2 on that pair. Read as its own session and pooled with the pair (--arm sessA,sessB:canon-c19-in12-sharp); the configuration is then the MEDIAN OF THREE. GOAL 3, THE LAST UNTRIED WILLINGNESS LEVER, ON A SETTLED BASE (user-ruled 2026-09-16: 'after the current config, go with one more 2+1 of your choice'; the choice and its reasoning are the agent's). The mod's third goal - a tech lead pushes laggards out - is the only one still unmet, and the shape of the miss is precise (F122, on this very base): rung 0 IS out-earned (a 22-26% margin against the frontier's 38-54%), its STAFFED levels fall by a fifth over the last three decades, and by 1935 it is 1% of either construction queue - but its LEVEL count still rises 12-18% from 1900, the growth front-loaded into 1900-1920, and half or more of the additions are NEW BUILDINGS in fresh states placed by countries that already hold the frontier (229 of 245, 287 of 304). Expansion below 80% staffing is forbidden by the engine, so what is left is placement, and placement is scored with noise. F120 closed the obvious lever: halving rung 0's own ai_value to 500 changed nothing, because the government AI's DESIRE is not what builds it - F100 identified the PRIVATE INVESTMENT POOL expanding company-owned buildings. THIS BOOK AIMS AT THAT ACTOR: PRODUCTION_BUILDING_RANDOM_FACTOR 10 -> 5 (the government AI's construction noise halved), PRODUCTION_BUILDING_AUTONOMOUS_INVESTMENT_RANDOM_FACTOR_MULT 2.0 -> 1.0 (the pool's noise quartered with it, since it multiplies the same factor) and PRODUCTION_BUILDING_AUTONOMOUS_INVESTMENT_PROFIT_FACTOR_MULT 1.5 -> 2.5 (the pool weighs predicted profit per employee more heavily). Willingness only - no hard block, per the standing ruling that build blocks are rejected as artificial. ⭐ WHY THIS BASE AND NOT AN EAGER ONE: canon-c19-in12 is SETTLED - four seeds at GDP 1.04 / 1.07 / 1.09 / 1.13x vanilla and workers per capita 0.64-0.70x, in band every time (F117 + F120) - whereas the eager family is mid-thread (F124: the spending thresholds cut the hoard to 0.11-0.34 but the four-define set read 0.74x and 1.45x). Testing a fine-grained willingness lever on a base that is about to be re-calibrated would confound it. The sharpening defines are orthogonal to the spending thresholds and can be combined later if both earn it.

_arms.canon-c19-in12-sharp: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.canon-c19-in12-sharp.json} - generated 2026-09-16 by make_ab_config from canon-c19-in12's own _ab.command with the three defines appended (its _ab.command holds the line); field diff against the base: ai_defines only, three keys, recorded twice; dry-run built clean; L20/L31 pass and L33 passes CLEAN (this book does not raise the land CRITICAL threshold, so it carries no ship-threshold residual).

_delta: Against canon-c19-in12 (the found configuration, F117 + F120): three AI defines, nothing else. No spending thresholds, no queue-cap change, every recipe, cost, ai_value, research event and the 24-month bar identical.

_predictions._structure: Pre-registered before launch, per the no-extrapolation rule. The KEY prediction is a within-run ratio over ~62k build decisions, which resolves at small n where GDP does not (F75).
_predictions.KEY_tier_choice: THE TEST: levels built BELOW the best tier the country already holds falls to under 25% of levels built, from the base's measured 34.9% (session 20260914_173832 run 1, same tool, same config). Anything at or above ~32% is a null result and closes the willingness line for goal 3 altogether - after F120 there is nothing else of this kind left to try.
_predictions.rung0: SECONDARY, and the one that matters for the goal itself: rung 0's 1935 level count at or below its 1900 count (the base rises 12-18%), fewer than 150 new rung-0 BUILDINGS added 1900 -> 1935 (the base 245 / 304, F122), and staffing under 40% at 1935 (the base 45-47%). ⚠ Read the STAFFED and BUILDING counts, never the level count alone - F122's lesson.
_predictions.gdp: world GDP 1.00-1.25x vanilla and workers per capita 0.62-0.75x - i.e. the base's band or a little above it, since sharper choice should raise the average building's return. The run-level stop applies: a run above 1.3x at 1936 ends the config.
_predictions.hoard: UNCHANGED from the base - world pool 0.42-0.70 of GDP, shortlist 0.61-1.50, Britain 0.87-2.40. This book carries none of the spending thresholds, so a hoard away from those numbers would mean the sharpening defines move the pool too, which nothing predicts.
_predictions.WATCH_the_failure_mode: A MONOTONE WORLD. Halving the noise that makes countries differ could simply make every country build the same thing, which would be a worse mod even with a better tier-choice number. Read `analyse_build_allocation.mjs --a <base run> --b <this run>` for the between-sector and between-industry shares ABSOLUTE as well as normalised (an industry whose share rises because everything else collapsed is not a win), the 'risk of disappearing' list at <0.60x, goods gluts, and `company_check.mjs` for formation and prosperity. A tier-choice win bought with a dead agricultural sector or a collapsed company layer is not a win.
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of the vanilla median; no crash expected, the feeder handles a mid-autosave CTD (L32).

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c19-in12-sharp` - world GDP and productive workers per capita at 1935 against the vanilla per-run median, five bands each; a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => the _tb.json as its own session, the reading the median of three. ⚠ THE ALIGNMENT CRITERIA ARE GDP AND WORKERS, NOT THE TIER-CHOICE NUMBER - the key prediction is a flag in the verdict, exactly as the rule says (no obsolescence criterion). PLUS THE RUN-LEVEL STOP and THE CAPITAL-ABUNDANCE FLAG (`capital_flags.mjs`, shortlist-wide = VOID, exit 4).
_comparison: vanilla n=18 for every ratio; canon-c19-in12 is the one-lever baseline and is settled at four seeds (F117 sessions 20260914_173832 + 20260914_204329, F120 session 20260915_082510): GDP 1.04 / 1.07 / 1.09 / 1.13x, workers 0.64-0.70x, below-best 34.9%, rung 0 45-47% staffed with its level count rising 12-18%, hoard 0.42-0.70 world.
_watch: every run ~5 min in: tools/testbed/batch_heartbeat.sh <session> - the mod marker, the version, this run's error window BY POSITION, the clock, CRASHED lines, and the DEFINE REJECTED alarm (L33: this book should show NO rejected define at all, unlike the eager family)
first run: analyse_ai_tier_choice.mjs (the key prediction), rung0_path.mjs + rung0_who.mjs, analyse_build_allocation.mjs against a base run, first_run_decomp.mjs, capital_flags.mjs, queue_series.mjs
post-run: alignment_check.mjs, capital_flags.mjs, company_check.mjs, preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger
_caveats: n=2 by design; the alignment tool decides on the third. The tier-choice ratio resolves far better than GDP at this n, which is why it is the key prediction.

Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent; the five-minute smoke check on EVERY run; never interleave configs.

The three defines have never been loaded by this project. They carry no stated bound in vanilla's comments and all three are ordinary positive multipliers, but L33's log half is what proves the engine took them - read the smoke check.
